name: Accessory Consistency
description: Analyzes accessory rendering consistency in video
mechanism:
This method analyzes temporal consistency of accessories (glasses, earrings, hats) across video frames for deepfake detection:

1. **Accessory Detection & Tracking**: Facial landmarks and object detection are used to identify accessories in each frame — glasses frames, earring positions, hat contours, and other wearable items. Each accessory is tracked across consecutive frames using optical flow and bounding box correlation.

2. **Geometric Consistency Analysis**: The geometric properties of detected accessories (shape, aspect ratio, symmetry) are measured per frame. In authentic video, accessories maintain consistent geometry modulated only by smooth head pose changes. Deepfakes often produce frame-to-frame geometric fluctuations in accessories due to imperfect face-swapping at boundaries.

3. **Texture & Appearance Stability**: Accessory surface textures (reflective properties of glasses lenses, metallic sheen of jewelry) are tracked. Real accessories show physically coherent appearance changes with lighting. Deepfake generators frequently fail to maintain consistent accessory rendering, producing flickering or morphing artifacts.

4. **Boundary Coherence Check**: The edges where accessories meet skin/hair are examined. Authentic boundaries show consistent occlusion relationships and natural blending. Face-swap artifacts typically produce irregular boundary rendering — glasses frames may partially merge with skin, or earrings may appear to clip through hair.

5. **Temporal Anomaly Scoring**: Statistical measures of accessory consistency (variance of geometric features, temporal gradient of appearance) are computed. High variance or sudden discontinuities across otherwise smooth motion sequences indicate manipulation, yielding an elevated forensic score.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through accessory consistency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
